content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic: ABIOC(KOI-010 Uncommon Shell Command Execution Under npm Install Hook Lineage) FOLLOWED_BY ABIOC(KOI-010 npm Install Hook Descendant Reads Multiple Developer Credential Files) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(KOI-010 Credentials Read And base64 Staged Under npm Install Lineage) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(KOI-010 Credential Archive Created Under npm Install Lineage) — all stitched by shared agent_hostname and actor_causality_id (CGO = the npm/node install process) so the lifecycle-hook detonation, multi-credential read, obfuscated staging and local archive collapse into ONE npm-supply-chain incident. The chain closes on the endpoint: its terminal term is the local archive create, not the egress, so the rule fires in a lab with no authorised sink and no firewall in path.
rules.name: npm Supply-Chain Credential Theft — Preinstall-Hook Detonation, Credential Harvest, Obfuscated Stage and Archive
